guide.title: Choking (Foreign Body Airway Obstruction)
guide.lead: Decide whether the cough is effective or not. If it is, leave it alone. If it isn't, act at once with back blows and thrusts, chosen by age and body type. If the patient goes limp, start CPR and look in the mouth each time you open the airway.

sections.title: Is the cough effective?
sections.question: Can they cough forcefully, speak or cry?
sections.yes: Mild obstruction: encourage coughing, don't interfere, monitor and transport.
sections.no: Severe obstruction (silent or weak cough, can't speak, stridor, cyanosis): act now.

sections.title: Severe obstruction: by patient

steps.text: 5 back blows between the shoulder blades, leaning them forward.
Repeat 5 + 5 until it clears or they become unresponsive.
Late pregnancy or obese: chest thrusts instead of abdominal thrusts.
Head down along your forearm: 5 back blows.
Turn over: 5 chest thrusts (two fingers, lower sternum).

sections.after: Becomes unresponsive: lower to the ground and start CPR. Each time you open the airway, look in the mouth and remove an object only if you can see it. No blind finger sweeps.

sections.title: After it clears
items: Anyone who needed abdominal thrusts should be checked for internal injury.
Persistent cough, difficulty swallowing or the feeling something is still there: assess in hospital.

quiz.q: A choking adult is coughing forcefully and can still speak. You should:
A responsive choking 6-month-old with a silent cough:
A choking adult becomes unresponsive. Next step?
options: Lower them to the ground and start CPR, looking in the mouth before breaths
quiz.explanation: Remove an object only if visible.

quiz.q: Severe obstruction in a responsive adult: current AHA/ERC sequence?
options: 5 back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts, repeated
quiz.explanation: Repeat until it clears or they become unresponsive.

quiz.q: A woman in late pregnancy is choking and can't speak. Instead of abdominal thrusts, use:

options: They can push the object deeper
quiz.explanation: Remove only what you can see.

options: Silent or weak cough and unable to speak

quiz.q: After successful abdominal thrusts, the patient feels fine. What do you advise?

options: With two fingers on the lower half of the sternum
With a fist on the abdomen
With the heel of the hand on the back

flashcards.question: Universal choking sign
flashcards.answer: Both hands clutching the throat, unable to speak or cough effectively.

flashcards.question: Mild obstruction
flashcards.answer: Effective cough: encourage coughing, do not interfere, monitor.

flashcards.question: Severe obstruction, adult or child over 1 year
flashcards.answer: 5 back blows then 5 abdominal thrusts, repeated until relieved or unresponsive.

flashcards.question: Severe obstruction, infant under 1 year
flashcards.answer: 5 back blows then 5 chest thrusts; never abdominal thrusts.

flashcards.question: Late pregnancy or obese
flashcards.answer: Chest thrusts instead of abdominal thrusts.

flashcards.question: Becomes unresponsive
flashcards.answer: Lower to the ground and start CPR; look in the mouth whenever you open the airway; remove only a visible object.

flashcards.question: Blind finger sweeps
flashcards.answer: No: they can push the object deeper.

flashcards.question: After abdominal thrusts
flashcards.answer: Check for internal injury, even if the patient feels well.

critical.scenario: At a restaurant a man stands up, clutches his throat, can't speak and is turning blue.
critical.question: Immediate action?

options.t: 5 back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts; repeat until it clears
Lay him down and start CPR

critical.kpi: Differentiates mild from severe FBAO and acts appropriately

critical.scenario: A woman 30 weeks pregnant is choking on food, can't speak and is panicking.
critical.question: Which technique?

options.t: Back blows, then chest thrusts instead of abdominal thrusts
Wait for her to cough it out

critical.kpi: Selects chest thrusts for the pregnant choking patient

critical.scenario: You are giving back blows to a choking infant. The infant goes limp.
critical.question: What next?

options.t: Start infant CPR; look in the mouth each time you open the airway and remove the object only if visible

critical.kpi: Transitions to CPR for the unresponsive choking infant
